SMTO-BOOT-0033 — The model server didn't start answering in time

GUID: f214d254-9f9b-4367-afdc-6d80104083c0
Slug: boot-model-readiness-timeout
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • SMTO's model tool waited for the model server, the program that runs the AI model, but it didn't answer before the time limit, or it closed while starting. Nothing was sent to the model yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Scroll up in the terminal where the model server was started and find its last error, for example running out of graphics memory or a missing model file. The time limit only shows that the server didn't answer; the server's own messages say why.
  2. Open the server's address in a web browser on the same computer: for Ollama, http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version; for the benchmark tool, the --base-url you gave it followed by /models. If it answers now, the server just needed longer; if nothing answers, it stopped or uses a different address.
  3. Before starting it again, make sure no other model server is still running or using the same port, for example with nvidia-smi, which lists programs using the graphics card. A second server can't use a busy port, and two servers can run the graphics card out of memory.
  4. If you use the benchmark tool and the model is large, add --server-timeout with a larger number of seconds, for example --server-timeout 300. The benchmark waits only 30 seconds by default, which may be too short for a big model to load.

What success looks like

  • The server's address answers in the browser (Ollama shows its version; a vLLM server lists the model), and the tool continues without this message.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the error line and the model server's last messages (for the benchmark tool, also the results report named on its "Results:" line), and send it to the person who manages your model setup. Don't start extra copies of the model server to get past this; check that the earlier one has fully stopped first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A model readiness poll gave up: the benchmark's wait_for_server got no successful GET of /v1/models before --server-timeout, or an Ollama launcher's own ollama serve did not answer /api/version within about 30 seconds or exited during startup.

What this means

  • Model endpoint polling reaches its readiness deadline without a successful response, or an Ollama launcher detects process exit while waiting. The readiness poll did not obtain a healthy response, or the Ollama process exited during startup. Ollama wrappers remove their temporary Modelfile and stop only a process they started. A timeout alone cannot identify a load error, insufficient memory, a wrong endpoint or a server that needs longer to start.

Why this can happen

  • Model endpoint polling reaches its readiness deadline without a successful response, or an Ollama launcher detects process exit while waiting.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect process state, endpoint and startup log before attributing failure to GPU memory.

How to fix it

  • Read the model server's own output for load, GPU memory or port-binding errors, and check the actual process and port state (for example ss -ltnp, curl on the benchmark's --base-url plus /models, or curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version) before starting another server. The benchmark polls only with --no-launch and gives up after --server-timeout (default 30 s), recording the error in its results report; the Ollama wrappers wait about 30 s, print a plain ERROR line, stop only a server they started and remove their temporary Modelfile.
  • Inspect the model server log for startup, device memory and endpoint errors.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the model server log and actual process/port state; resolve the startup or endpoint problem before starting another server.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended server remains running and answers the supported readiness endpoint.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The readiness poll did not obtain a healthy response, or the Ollama process exited during startup. Ollama wrappers remove their temporary Modelfile and stop only a process they started.
  • A timeout alone cannot identify a load error, insufficient memory, a wrong endpoint or a server that needs longer to start.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
